title: Engineering & IT
summary: Applied programs in AI, computer science, electronics and engineering — with strong lab facilities.
overview: China is one of the largest markets for engineering education. Universities invest in labs, and companies co-run programs and internships. Admission depends not only on grades but on projects, maths and motivation.
Most bachelor's programs are Chinese-taught; English-taught options are more common at master's level. If you want to work as an engineer in China, plan to build Chinese alongside your degree.
fitFor: Strong maths and relevant school subjects
You have projects, competitions or work experience
You're interested in AI, embedded systems, energy or electronics
You want labs and internships, not only lectures
outcomes: A portfolio of lab and applied projects
An internship at a technology company
A foundation for work in Asia and international teams

timeline.text: We match your profile to programs and labs and check maths requirements.
We prepare transcripts, a CV, a project portfolio, references and language certificates.

faq.question: Do I need IELTS for an engineering master's?
faq.answer: For English-taught programs, often yes, but some universities accept previous study in English or run an internal test. We check requirements per program.

faq.question: Can I get into an IT master's without a relevant degree?
faq.answer: Sometimes, if you have strong maths and a portfolio, but most programs expect a relevant degree or a close field. That's why we build the academic profile before choosing universities.
